review.decision: Stage only in memory until the final dispatch gate and make the stable ID and initial directory part of durable authorization.
review.notes: P1.3 plus the independent P1.4 blocker 86f8150a. Go and DSH share the same index contract; old v1 pending without an index key must resolve a unique matching index in a bounded scan. Index unlink failure must retain the durable receipt. Unknown, unstable and partially written evidence is preserved. Tests are isolated and not a simulation of target-media power loss. Final-head CI review verified the injected error sentinel rename preserves all existing fault assertions.

cases.description: Draft, waiting, duplicate and late hold do not consume durable input slots.
cases.setup: Private empty or preexisting legacy queue, staged DSH and Codex input, injected composer and final native gate.
cases.action: Refuse submissions repeatedly before and after paste; inspect queue and lock names. Publish a winning intent, race a second attempt for the same ID and retry an old pending or accepted ID. Verify old age-out for settled non-durable attempts and stable replay protection for durable IDs.
cases.expected: Drafts and gates create no durable slot, and the final authorizer publishes only its staged ID. Failed contenders do not replace a previous index. Aged unresolved requests cannot be replaced by force or timeout. A durable accepted ID remains idempotent.

cases.description: Index and initial directory survive the durability boundary before a receiver can mutate.
cases.setup: Private HOME with fresh or existing queue, injected index/parent/queue synchronization faults, actual shipped DSH synthetic receiver.
cases.action: Block initial directory sync, index write/flush and index publication; retry a committed input through a new intent; remove or damage old DSH index; interrupt retirement at index deletion.
cases.expected: No pending is claimable before a synced bound index, and no followup occurs without it. Existing v1 is accepted only with a unique matched index. A retained stable mapping returns the same known result. The terminal receipt survives an index deletion failure, and no unknown data is discarded.
